question.:question/problem:
If the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $1,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of ${210}^{∘}$ with the positive $x$-axis, then the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$, where

$$
r=1,\,\theta ={210}^{∘}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({210}^{∘}) \\  & =1\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡({210}^{∘}) \\  & =1\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},-\frac{1}{2}).$
